make.name: Zeekr
make.description: Premium electric-car brand set up by Geely in March 2021, selling in China, Europe, Australia and much of Asia. Zeekr took control of Lynk & Co in February 2025, and Geely Auto took Zeekr private in December 2025, delisting it from the New York Stock Exchange.

logo.license: Public domain (Wikimedia Commons); trademark of Zeekr

models.description: Zeekr's first car: a large electric shooting brake on Geely's SEA platform, on sale in China since October 2021 and in Europe since 2023. It was facelifted with an 800V system in February 2024 and updated again with 103 kWh packs in October 2025.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Launch version with 86 or 100 kWh CATL packs (140 kWh Qilin option from 2023) and 200 kW RWD or 400 kW dual-motor AWD.

generations.name: 2024 facelift
generations.description: February 2024 facelift: new exterior, 800V architecture, 95 kWh LFP or 100 kWh NMC packs and 580 kW dual-motor AWD.

generations.name: 2026 model year
generations.description: October 2025 update: 103 kWh NMC pack, a 370 kW rear motor and 680 kW dual-motor AWD.

models.description: Mid-size electric sedan on an 800V architecture, launched in December 2023. The April 2026 update raised motor output and added a 103 kWh pack.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Launch version: 75 kWh LFP or 100 kWh NMC packs, 310 kW RWD or 475 kW dual-motor AWD.

generations.name: 2026 update
generations.description: April 2026 update: 370 kW rear motor, 585 kW dual-motor AWD and a 103 kWh NMC long-range pack.

models.name: 007 GT
models.description: Shooting-brake (estate) version of the 007, launched in China in April 2025 and sold abroad as the Zeekr 7GT.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Launch version: 75 kWh LFP or 100 kWh NMC, 310 kW RWD or 475 kW AWD.

generations.name: 2026 update
generations.description: April 2026 update with the 007's 370 kW / 585 kW motors and a 103 kWh NMC long-range pack.

models.description: Large luxury electric MPV with six or seven seats (four in the Grand), deliveries from early 2023. The July 2024 update moved to an 800V 108 kWh pack and added front-drive and 140 kWh versions.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Launch version: 400 kW dual-motor AWD with a 116 kWh NMC or 140 kWh Qilin pack.

generations.name: 2024 update
generations.description: July 2024 update: 108 kWh 800V NMC pack with 580 kW AWD or 310 kW FWD, plus 140 kWh FWD/AWD and the four-seat Grand.

models.name: X
models.description: Compact electric crossover on the SEA platform (related to the smart #1 and Volvo EX30), launched in 2023 in China and Europe. A facelift with new 61 kWh LFP and 66 kWh NMC packs arrived for the 2026 model year (November 2025).

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Launch version: 66 kWh NMC pack with 200 kW RWD or about 315 kW dual-motor AWD; a 49 kWh LFP RWD was added in China for the 2025 model year.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: 2026 model-year facelift: 61 kWh LFP (RWD) and 66 kWh NMC (AWD) packs, peak output 250 to 365 kW, CLTC 512 to 560 km.

models.name: 7X
models.description: Mid-size electric SUV launched in China in September 2024 and in Europe, Australia and Asia from 2025. The October 2025 facelift brought stronger motors and a 103 kWh pack.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Launch version: 75 kWh LFP or 100 kWh NMC, 310 kW RWD or 475 kW dual-motor AWD.

generations.name: 2026 model-year facelift
generations.description: October 2025 facelift: 370 kW rear motor, 585 kW AWD, 103 kWh pack on a 900V system.

models.name: Mix
models.description: Compact five-seat electric MPV with sliding doors and a pillarless side, launched in China in October 2024.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Only generation; 310 kW rear motor, 76 kWh LFP or 102 kWh NMC.

models.name: Ojai (Waymo robotaxi)
models.description: Purpose-built robotaxi developed with Waymo from the M-Vision concept, shown as the Zeekr RT and renamed Waymo Ojai in January 2026. It is not sold to the public; Waymo began carrying riders in it in 2026.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Base vehicles built by Zeekr in Ningbo from December 2024 and fitted with Waymo hardware in Arizona.

gaps: No legacy rows exist for Zeekr; make is new to the site.
